content.title: Add a task
content.description: A user adds a new task to the todo list by entering a task title and submitting it with Enter, with the source defining the title input and Enter key submission as the promised creation path.
content.summary: Create a new task from a typed title.
content.value: Lets users capture a new todo item in the list with minimal effort.
criteria: A task is added from a typed task title when the user presses Enter.

content.title: Complete a task
content.description: A user marks an existing task complete by clicking its checkbox, with completion reflected as the completed task state and a strikethrough presentation called out by the source.
content.value: Lets users track which tasks are finished without removing them from the list.
criteria: Clicking a checkbox marks a task complete.
Completed tasks use a strikethrough style.

content.title: Delete a task
content.description: A user removes an existing task from the todo list by clicking the task's "x" control, with the source defining deletion as a direct action on the task card.
content.summary: Remove an existing task from the list.
content.value: Lets users discard tasks that are no longer needed.
criteria: Deleting a task is triggered by clicking an "x" control on the task.

content.title: Resume tasks after page reload
content.description: A user returns to the application after a page reload and finds their tasks still present, with the source explicitly promising persistence across reloads via localStorage.
content.summary: Keep tasks available after reloading the page.
content.value: Prevents task loss and avoids re-entry after a refresh or reopen.

content.title: See a task's priority
content.description: A user sees each task card display a small priority badge while the existing card UI, controls, and layout otherwise remain unchanged, with the source specifying High, Medium, and Low values and a default of Medium but no priority-editing flow.
content.summary: View the priority shown on each task card.
content.value: Helps users distinguish task importance without changing the existing task card interaction model.
criteria: Each task card shows a small priority badge and the rest of the card UI, controls, and layout stay unchanged.
Priority values are High, Medium, and Low, and the default is Medium.
